packages/agent-host/src/messaging-inboun.reason: Regression coverage for the inbound command path keeps the link, routing, replay guard, poll-cursor durability, poll-loop and endpoint-rule contracts in one suite beside the module they exercise, because each contract is a facet of the same receive loop; the ceiling moved from 983 to 1127 when the crash-window ordering, the backwards-cursor guard, the audited cursor-save failure, the guard record-point ordering and the IPv4-mapped-literal refusals each gained a case. It moved from 1127 to 1147 for the session-ownership work (ADR 0325): the fixture session records the linked principal as its owner, mirroring the post-bind state a real bound conversation has, and one case proves the linked principal is refused while the row is unowned and admitted once it owns the session. Both are facets of the same routing contract this suite already owns.

The inbound command path (ADR 0205 D375 item 9, ADR 0326) keeps the link reader, receive-loop driver, replay guard, cursor handling and the transport seam in one sidecar-private source boundary: the driver, its cursor and its guard only mean anything next to each other, the guard's record-point and the cursor's save-point are the same ordering decision seen from two sides, and the transport's endpoint rule is the boundary the driver's credential depends on. The ceiling moved from 874 to 896 when the Forward-API note was replaced by the wiring note and that note was then made true: the wiring note names the factory in host-runtime, the ports it injects, the persisted binding, the production binding writer (`bindMessagingInboundSession`, behind the host-internal bind IPC channel); it also states the loop's shutdown precisely — the signal is re-checked between iterations, so a single in-flight iteration can outlive the abort by one host RPC deadline, which is why each root bounds its await. The note was then corrected again in place, at the same size, when the session-ownership work (ADR 0325) made its claim that this module performs no ownership check and the wiring adds none false: the module still performs none, but the Host now does, and the target resolver reads its snapshot under the acting principal so that rule applies before a target is built. The ceiling moved from 896 to 982 for the Slack inbound transport union (ADR 0326): the receive shape is generalized to a pull transport (Telegram's long poll, unchanged) or a push transport (Slack's Socket Mode), told apart structurally so every existing Telegram transport object is still a pull transport; `readInboundLink` gains two optional format/version parameters defaulting to Telegram's, so a second channel reuses the one fail-closed reader rather than restating it; and `run` gains the push branch. The driver, its cursor, its guard and the transport union still have to be read together — the Slack client itself, its envelope unwrap, its filters and its durable replay guard live in `messaging-slack-inbound.ts` and are not in this file — so the file is not split here.
